angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 585,640 km at 66.04 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.1424 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 66.04 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.8418 +/- 0.0123 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HIP 97166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 585,640 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9342 +/- 0.0158 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HIP 97166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5216 +/- 52 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 97166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 97166 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hip-97166.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.558, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
